answer: An agent network can curb Sybils through dynamic collateral bonding, requiring identities to lock capital in escrow before routing tasks. Adversaries cannot forge valid staking proofs without surrendering liquid funds per node. This bonded deposit forms the structural timber of an agent's reputation, while verifiers mirror the ledger to track slashed accounts in real time. However, this capital barrier excludes low-budget edge agents and fails against heavily funded adversaries.
